# Music prompts for Suno (T-061, T-133)

Every track below is four boxes that each paste whole into Suno's Custom mode: **Title**, **Style of music**, **Lyrics** and **Exclude styles** (Suno's name for the negative prompt). Nothing needs combining or editing: copy the text in each box as it stands. Keep the file name, the target length and the notes with the master you keep.

**Status (2026-10-06):** tracks 1 to 6 (`title`, `farm_spring`, `farm_summer`, `farm_fall`, `farm_winter`, `farm_night`) were generated by the owner from earlier versions of these prompts and are in the game (`Assets/_Project/Resources/Music/`, played by `MusicDirector`; the source files are in `audio/`). Paste them again only to regenerate. Tracks 7 to 18 (`village`, `saloon`, `library`, `indoors`, `forest`, `beach`, `mine`, `rain`, `festival_spring`, `festival_summer`, `festival_fall`, `festival_winter`) were generated on 2026-10-09 and are in the game too (`MusicChoice` says where each plays). Tracks 19 and later (`heart_event`, `performance`, the stingers and the horror layer) do not exist yet.

## How to use
1. In Suno choose **Custom**, switch **Instrumental** on, then paste: Title into *Song Title*, the first code block into *Styles*, the second into *Lyrics* (the tags keep it instrumental and give the shape), the third into *Exclude Styles* (under *More Options*).
2. Generate two to four versions of each. Keep the one whose last bar leads back into its first (loops) or that ends cleanly (stingers, festivals, endings); trim on a bar line in an editor.
3. Export WAV if the plan allows, otherwise the highest-rate MP3. The game imports Ogg Vorbis: convert once and keep the master.
4. The cue name is the file name (`farm_spring.ogg`) that scenes and the audio director use (the `music` event step, `MusicCue`).

## Rules that apply to every prompt
- No artist, band, composer or game names anywhere (originality rule; Suno also rejects artist names). Check any edit you make against this.
- One world: the same palette (nylon and steel-string guitar, upright piano, harmonium or pump organ, fiddle, tin whistle, mandolin, glockenspiel, upright bass, brushed snare, hand percussion, cello), keys in the D major, G major and B minor family, and one short recurring motif (a rising fourth, then a step down) in the title, farm and village themes.
- Licence and ownership depend on the Suno plan used: record the plan and each track's generation date in `docs/ASSET_LICENSES.md` before a track is committed.
- If the Styles box rejects a prompt as too long on an older model, delete the words after the first two commas of the palette part; the box takes about 1000 characters on current models.

## Mythos layer (only at horror intensity mild or full; at off the game uses the cozy tracks)
Restrained and uncanny, never gory, no jump scares. The Keepers protect the world, so their music is solemn and ceremonial, not villainous. The same acoustic palette as the cozy score, detuned and thinned out, so it sounds like the same world at night. These tracks belong with the horror layer (`Farm.Mythos` and data), not the core assemblies. At mild the same pieces play; none contains explicit ritual imagery or harsh sounds.

## After generating
1. Pick, trim and loop-check each track; keep the master with its prompt and the generation date.
2. Name files after the cue (`farm_spring.ogg` ...) and put them under `Assets/_Project/Audio/Music/` once the audio pass (T-061) defines the layout.
3. Update `docs/ASSET_LICENSES.md` (source, plan, date) before any track is committed.
4. Listen for melodies that resemble an existing piece and regenerate those rather than ship them.
